result: The authors generated split-GAL4 driver lines targeting central complex cell types, including 52 new high-quality lines with expression largely limited to the cell type of interest, achieving coverage of nearly one-third of CX cell types at high quality and more than three-quarters overall.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly praised this work. Reviewer 2 stated 'The description of dozens of cell-specific split-GAL4 lines is extremely valuable to the fly community' and emphasized these are 'fantastic tools.' Reviewer 1 noted the work 'contributes new, useful and systematic technical information in compelling fashion.' The editor described this as part of 'a fundamental body of work' with tools that 'will undoubtedly serve as a foundation for future studies.'

result: Using EASI-FISH, the authors characterized expression patterns of 41 neuropeptides and 18 neuropeptide receptors in the adult central brain, finding that about half of neuropeptides were expressed in only a few cells while the rest were expressed in dozens to hundreds of cells, with receptors expressed more broadly and at lower levels, and that 51 of 85 CX cell types examined expressed at least one neuropeptide.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly endorsed this work. Reviewer 2 stated 'The description of neurotransmitter/neuropeptides expression pattern in the CX is of remarkable importance and will help design experiments aimed at understanding how the CX functions.' The editor noted 'findings, which include characterization of neuromodulators used by different cells, will undoubtedly serve as a foundation for future studies.' No concerns were raised about the EASI-FISH methodology or neuropeptide expression findings.

result: All neuropeptide-expressing CX cell types co-expressed a small molecule neurotransmitter (most often acetylcholine or glutamate), while co-transmission of two fast-acting transmitters was rare, but co-transmission of a fast-acting transmitter with modulatory transmitters like serotonin was common.
evaluation: This finding was highlighted by reviewers as important. Reviewer 2 emphasized 'The description of neurotransmitter/neuropeptides expression pattern in the CX is of remarkable importance.' The editor noted the characterization of neuromodulators as a key contribution. No reviewer questioned these co-transmission findings or the underlying data.

result: Specific neurotransmitter identities were determined for individual cell types: PFG neurons use tyramine (expressing Tdc2 but not Tbh), and FB4K neurons co-express acetylcholine and glutamate.
evaluation: These specific examples of neurotransmitter characterization were part of the broader neuropeptide/neurotransmitter mapping that reviewers praised. Reviewer 2 stated the neurotransmitter expression pattern description is 'of remarkable importance.' No concerns were raised about these specific cell type characterizations.

result: The authors identified multiple CX cell types that affect sleep/wake behavior through thermogenetic and optogenetic activation, including strongly wake-promoting cell types (hDeltaF, SMP368, SMP531) and others with varying effects (PEN_b, PFGs, EL, hDeltaK), with many showing sexually dimorphic phenotypes.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly stated 'I find the behavioral (sleep) screen of this manuscript to be incomplete' and noted 'There is no silencing data and/or assessment of sleep homeostasis or arousal threshold.' The reviewer acknowledged 'this manuscript will pave the way for further studies' but emphasized the screen 'seems to be unfinished and could have been more matured.' Reviewer 2 also noted 'it is possible that the activation protocols used in this study are insufficient for some neuronal types' and that mild activation protocols may have 'missed some phenotypes.'

result: The authors identified connectivity pathways linking clock outputs to the CX through cell types like SMP368 and SMP531, and found that ER5 cells express receptors for PDF and Dh44 and make Dh31, with many intrinsic CX cell types showing sleep phenotypes being connected by wired pathways revealed in the connectome.
evaluation: While the behavioral screen was critiqued as incomplete, the connectivity analysis and receptor expression findings were not questioned. The editor noted the work includes 'anatomical, molecular, and functional mapping' and reviewers praised the systematic characterization. The connectivity data complementing the behavioral findings was implicitly accepted as part of the overall contribution.

result: The authors characterized six CX cell types by RNA profiling, with results largely congruent with EASI-FISH data.
evaluation: This RNA profiling work was part of the broader molecular characterization that reviewers praised. Reviewer 1 noted the work 'continues to set a high and transparent standard by which large-scale resources can be defined and shared.' No concerns were raised about the RNA profiling methodology or its concordance with EASI-FISH.

result: The authors used three metrics to assess sleep (sleep duration, P(Doze), P(Wake)) and tested multiple independent driver lines for most cell types, assaying all lines in both males and females with both thermogenetic and optogenetic activation, observing sexually dimorphic phenotypes and finding that activation of hDeltaF does not increase activity measures.
evaluation: While Reviewer 2 critiqued the behavioral screen as incomplete, the methodology itself was not questioned. The reviewer acknowledged the authors 'have performed neuronal activation using thermogenetic and/or optogenetic approaches' and noted 'Lines that showed strong effects generally did so with both activation modes.' The systematic approach of testing both sexes and multiple lines was implicitly accepted.

result: Background claims about the central complex: it consists of approximately 2800 cells divided into 257 cell types, plays a key role in sensory-motor information flow, is important in orientation and navigation, participates in sleep/activity regulation, and is one of the most peptidergic brain areas.
evaluation: These are established background facts supported by citations to published literature. No reviewer questioned these foundational claims about the CX. They serve as context for the study's contributions.
